title: Are Knowledge and Reference in Multilingual Language Models Cross-Lingually Consistent?

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the cross-lingual consistency of factual knowledge retrieval by comparing output probability distributions (Top@1 Accuracy and RankC) and contextualized representation similarity (CKA) between original monolingual statements and code-mixed coreferential statements (where the subject entity is substituted with its translation in another language). The paper also uses activation patching based on Integrated Gradients (IG2) to intervene in feed-forward network layers and measure the causal effect of language bias on model consistency.
